# City of Burlington municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 4; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists Emma Mulvaney-Stanak as Mayor of Burlington.
City of Burlington charter, Title 24 Appendix V.S.A. chapter 003: sections 3(a) and 125(a) provide for election of a Mayor for a three-year term.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists twelve Burlington City Councilors: Mark Barlow (North District), Eugene Bergman (Ward 2), Marek Broderick (Ward 8), Sarah Carpenter (Ward 4), Melo Grant (Central District), Evan Litwin (Ward 7), Becca McKnight (Ward 6), Carter Neubieser (Ward 1), Laura Sanchez-Parkinson (Ward 3), Allie Schachter (East District), Ranjot "Buddy" Singh (South District), and Ben Traverse (Ward 5; Council President).
City of Burlington charter, Title 24 Appendix V.S.A. chapter 003: sections 3(b) and 125(b) provide for election of four district councilors and eight ward councilors, all for two-year terms.

City of Burlington, 'Declaration of Election Results - Candidates (Official)' for the March 3, 2026 Annual City Election: declares the eight ward councilors elected March 3, 2026: Carter Neubieser (Ward 1), Gene Bergman (Ward 2), Laura Sanchez-Parkinson (Ward 3), Sarah Carpenter (Ward 4), Ben Traverse (Ward 5), Becca Brown McKnight (Ward 6), Evan Litwin (Ward 7), and Marek Broderick (Ward 8). The four district councilors were elected in 2025 and stand from the Secretary of State directory.

City of Burlington charter, Title 24 Appendix V.S.A. chapter 003: section 122(a) provides that the Mayor appoints a Chief Administrative Officer with the approval of the City Council, and section 138 assigns the officer the functions of the former City Clerk and City Treasurer; the charter has no elected clerk or treasurer.
City of Burlington official website, Staff Directory: styles Katherine Schad 'Chief Administrative Officer', Clerk / Treasurer's Office.

City of Burlington charter, Title 24 Appendix V.S.A. chapter 003: sections 122(a) and 151 provide for a City Grand Juror appointed by the Mayor with the approval of the City Council. The city publishes no current holder by name, so the post is created structure only.

City of Burlington charter, Title 24 Appendix V.S.A. chapter 003: sections 122(a) and 152 provide for a City Constable appointed by the Mayor with the approval of the City Council. The city publishes no current holder by name, so the post is created structure only.
City of Burlington charter, Title 24 Appendix V.S.A. chapter 003: section 10 provides for election of one Ward Clerk in each of the city's eight wards, for a two-year term.
City of Burlington official website, 'Election Workers - Ward Clerks & Inspectors of Election' page: describes the ward clerk office but publishes no names by ward.

City of Burlington, 'Declaration of Election Results - Candidates (Official)' for the March 3, 2026 Annual City Election: shows a Ward Clerk line only for Ward 3, marked 'No candidate elected'. No current ward clerk roster is published, so all eight seats are left unfilled. Structure only.
City of Burlington charter, Title 24 Appendix V.S.A. chapter 003: section 10 provides for election of three Inspectors of Election in each of the city's eight wards, for staggered three-year terms.

City of Burlington, 'Declaration of Election Results - Candidates (Official)' for the March 3, 2026 Annual City Election: declares the Inspectors of Election elected March 3, 2026: Linda A. Sheehey (Ward 1), Julia DiPietro (Ward 2), Deborah Krugipudi (Ward 3, two-year term), Wendy Rice (Ward 4), Rachel Fisher (Ward 5), Leslyn Hall (Ward 6), and Thomas L. Fleury (Ward 7); the Ward 3 three-year seat and both Ward 8 seats are marked 'No candidate elected'. Inspectors elected in the 2024 and 2025 cycles are published in no current roster; those seats are left unfilled rather than reconstructed from past declarations.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen Burlington justices of the peace: Sue Alenick, Carmen George, Dawn Ellis, Andrew D. Champagne, Mary-Katherine Stone, Robert "Bob" Bolyard, Erin Kranichfeld, Theresa Lefebvre, Amanda Janoo, Helaine "Lainey" Rappaport, Robert Hooper, Owen Doherty, Ryan Nick, Zoraya Hightower, and Gene Bergman.
